newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures dip at end of dull session.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures dip at end of dull session.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended slightly easier on Thursday after remaining stuck within a range established in early trade.

Dealers said interest continued to be hampered by concerns about a Japanese economic slowdown and uncertainty about the new government after the Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) failed to win a majority in Sunday's general election.

"The initial slide started on Monday with the idea that an increase in the consumption tax is on its way," said a dealer with a U.S. futures house, referring to the LDP's plan to hike the consumption tax from the current three percent to five percent next April.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 December contract ended at 21,060 against 21,085 previously on low volume of 14,585 lots.

"It looks like we're pretty steady above 21,000, which is a good sign," said the dealer, adding that the market could end the week on a firmer note if players covered their short positions on Friday, but the overall trend looked bearish.
